motion.name: duration
motion.purpose: The --duration token for hover, press and colour transitions; 0ms under prefers-reduced-motion.

motion.name: ease-entrance
motion.purpose: Every entrance and pulse on the stage: rise, toast-in, summon-rise, banner, mic-pulse.

motion.name: rise
motion.purpose: Prediction card enters from 24px below at 97% scale.

motion.name: toast-in
motion.purpose: Discovery toast slides up 40px.

motion.name: summon-rise
motion.purpose: Authored Studio entrance: guide rises from 60vh at 60% scale with a 4% overshoot at 60%.

motion.name: spell-burst
motion.purpose: Sunshine radial pool scales 0.2 to 1.6 and fades.

motion.name: banner
motion.purpose: Spell banner pops to 105%, holds, drifts up 10px and fades.

motion.name: mic-pulse
motion.purpose: Sunshine ring breathes 94% to 110% and fades; 1.4s on the speaking friend.

motion.name: chip-pulse
motion.purpose: Connected status dot throws a 9px sunshine halo.

motion.name: dot
motion.purpose: Three building dots bounce 8px with 150ms stagger.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.purpose: CSS decorative loops are removed and entrances collapse; the shared actor model retains semantic action/speech poses while suppressing idle blink and repeated gestures/swimming.

motion.name: learn-tooth-blink
motion.purpose: Twinkle blink pose overlay; removed with reduced motion.

motion.name: learn-tooth-brush
motion.purpose: Alternate two authored brushing frames; removed with reduced motion.

motion.name: learn-tooth-arrive
motion.purpose: Celebration pose arrives from 3px below at 98% scale; removed with reduced motion.

motion.name: learn-story-arrive
motion.purpose: Story celebration arrival; removed with reduced motion. The completion-to-ending delay is 850ms, or zero with reduced motion.

motion.name: actor-clock
motion.purpose: Shared visible-actor sampler; skips offscreen actors and stops when all are offscreen or the document is hidden. No per-actor RAF or React frame rendering.

motion.name: actor-blink
motion.purpose: Staggered single blink pose; disabled with reduced motion.

motion.name: actor-speech
motion.purpose: Real playback amplitude selects one opaque small/open speech pose on the matching voice owner; Studio/companion ownership uses VoiceClient.speakerId. Semantic speech remains under reduced motion; not phoneme lip-sync.

motion.name: actor-action-window
motion.purpose: Listen/rest and requested gestures expire; wave uses 220ms pose steps and dance/bounce 280ms steps, settling sooner. Celebration holds its semantic result pose. Reduced motion retains representative poses without repeated gestures.

motion.name: actor-aquatic-request
motion.purpose: Dolphin, Whale, Seal and Penguin swim requests use the existing Ocean cycle. Reduced motion selects a semantic pose. Distance-driven route/trail locomotion remains separate.

motion.name: learn-tooth-speaking
motion.purpose: Unchanged ToothActor alone retains amplitude-driven speaking-pose opacity.

appearance.scope: Published semantic interface/brand palette presets. Preserve default frontmatter tokens, Dream Launch geometry and original character/subject pixels; no arbitrary CSS or custom logo inputs.

publication.concurrency: Compare supplied revision in transaction; stale revision returns 409.
publication.refresh: Current publisher updates immediately; other visible pages poll every 30000ms and refresh on focus or visibility return.
publication.fallback: Last valid cached palette, otherwise Forest.
publication.icons: lib/brand.ts SVG browser icon; theme-manifest and public/icons/themes/<theme>/{icon-192,icon-512,maskable,apple}.png. Installed updates depend on platform caching.

utilityIcons.semantics: Decorative SVG inside a labelled button/link; accessible name and target belong to the control.
utilityIcons.removed: Decorative sparkle badges, summon particles, guide-name sparks and idle Studio particle orb.
utilityIcons.retained: Semantic reward stars, five-point brand star, celestial subject art and contained live voice feedback.
utilityIcons.liveFeedback: DotOrb mounts only when live; 100% portrait footprint. Compact <=280px container uses an 84–140px portrait column separate from copy.

narrative.northStar: The Theatre Built From the Mark
narrative.overview:
Just Imagine has a default Forest palette and two rooms. The parent room is a calm, paper-coloured page: warm cream ground (#fff9ee), deep green foreground (#243e36), forest actions (#245e4e), muted leaf, ochre and clay accents. Locally hosted Baloo provides soft rounded headings; Nunito provides readable body copy. The landing composition pairs a large question with an abstract geometric play window. It makes no claim that geometric placeholders are final illustration.

The child room is the same palette turned inside out. The Studio is a stage, not a page: the forest green that is ink on the parent side becomes the wings and floor, and the cream that is ground on the parent side becomes the pills, captions and sheets that float at the stage edges. The Dream Launch mark (forest tile, cream cloud, peach arc, sunshine star) supplies the whole stage vocabulary: forest for the house, cream for anything you can touch, peach for warmth, sunshine for anything live. The six preset friends and guides now carry their established identities into tactile registered raster poses inside the same SVG slots; optional external Rive assets retain their existing mounting path.

Learning Worlds adds the user-approved Tooth Town craft to this theatre: tactile sculpted characters, expressive acting poses, soft key and rim lighting, and eight active cinematic environments across nine story adventures. The warm cream-and-forest shell stays familiar. Learn’s rounded rectangular controls, painted scenery and scene gradients remain scoped to Learn. The Tooth Town acting standard now also covers the six preset Studio friends/guides and eight pets through shared registered raster presentation; identities, mounting slots and the optional Rive path remain intact.

The child and parent worlds share typography and semantic colors. Interface transition duration becomes zero with reduced-motion preferences; shared actor presentation retains semantic poses and audio-driven speech while removing repeated gestures and idle blinks. Physics remains interactive. Parent forms and all actionable child controls retain visible keyboard focus. Browser selection, progress meters and range inputs use the same palette.

The user authorized the Forest/Ocean/Terracotta preset extension and coordinated recolouring of existing brand/browser/install icons. Semantic interface roles change together; tactile artwork and brand geometry remain. Shared rounded-stroke controls replace decorative sparkle UI. Idle Studio portraits have no particle orb; live feedback stays inside its portrait column. Appearance uses a separate draft preview and explicit audited, revision-checked publication.
keyCharacteristics: One coordinated palette, inverted between rooms: Forest is the warm cream-and-forest default; authorized Ocean and Terracotta presets preserve the same semantic roles.
Baloo for anything that names (headings, dial values, chip titles, answer buttons); Nunito for anything that explains (body, captions, pill labels).
Sunshine (#f7d76e) means live: mic ring, speaking friend's ring, pressed pill, connected dot, active challenge, spell banner.
Fully rounded pills on the stage; 10 to 16 px corners in the parent room.
Soft offset shadows cast toward the floor; no borders on the stage, quiet 1 px dividers in the parent room.

The Studio summon remains its authored entrance; predefined Learn characters, preset friends/guides and pets share anchored pose changes, while Learn retains distance-driven locomotion and causal game feedback.
Tooth Town’s tactile character craft extends across predefined actors; cream controls and forest structure keep the shared interface legible through stories, Studio, navigation and pets.

rules.name: The Sunshine-Means-Live Rule
rules.body: Yellow (#f7d76e) is reserved for things that are listening, speaking, pressed, connected, or just happened. It never decorates a resting surface. A yellow element the child cannot act on or that is not currently happening is a defect.

rules.name: The Inverted Rooms Rule
rules.body: The selected preset supplies both rooms: ink on ground for parents, ground on ink for the stage. Forest remains the default; publish Ocean or Terracotta as coordinated presets, not page-specific palettes.

rules.name: The Quiet Chrome Rule
rules.body: On the stage, controls that leave or reset (home, gallery, reset) are translucent cream at 15% on forest; controls that act in the world (captions, finish, answers) are opaque cream or a full accent. A child should be able to tell "exit" from "play" by weight alone.

rules.name: The Naming Face Rule
rules.body: Baloo appears wherever a thing is named or chosen: headings, dial values, variable names, answer buttons, keypad digits, the spell banner. Nunito appears wherever a thing is explained: body, captions, pill labels, hints. A Baloo sentence or a Nunito heading is a defect.

rules.name: The Sentence Case Rule
rules.body: No uppercase labels anywhere. Small labels get Baloo weight and a darker colour, not tracking or capitals.

rules.name: The Stage-Not-Page Rule
rules.body: The Studio never scrolls and never shows a heading over the world. The world fills the viewport and everything else floats at the edges in pills.

rules.name: The Beside-Not-Over Rule
rules.body: The lab column and the cast strip share the viewport with the world; they never cover it. Only transient moments (prediction, summon, spell, toast) may overlay the world, and each one is dismissed by a child's answer or by time.

rules.name: The Floor Shadow Rule
rules.body: Shadows always fall downward with negative spread and never spread outward evenly. A centred glow, a hard offset, or a coloured halo on a resting surface is a defect; the only radial light pools are the cream spotlight behind the listening friend and the sunshine burst of a spell, and both are moments, not surfaces.

rules.name: The Line-Or-Shadow Rule
rules.body: The parent room separates with lines and never with shadows on content; the stage separates with shadows and never with lines. The single exception is the 1 px cream line at 13% along the top of the cast strip.

rules.name: The Acting-Sheet Rule
rules.body: Keep each character’s identity, proportions, scale and registration consistent across its states. Shared gesture poses use their registered bottom anchor; dedicated swimming/flying locomotion uses a body center. Select one opaque authored pose and route speech to its playback owner; whole-character bobbing and blended faces do not fulfill the acting direction. Bound requested gestures, pause invisible/hidden actor updates and retain semantic states under reduced motion. Advance travel locomotion by actual distance, stop it at rest and preserve legal route corners. Keep crops within their cells and retain the separate coach matching sheet’s measured row bounds.

rules.name: The Causal-Play Rule
rules.body: A learning scene must expose a direct action and a visible consequence. Artwork supplies atmosphere; native hit targets, paths, phase geometry and progress carry the game’s meaning. A facts panel is an optional conversation, not the primary game.

dos: Do keep both rooms on the selected semantic palette: ink on ground for parents, ground on ink for the stage; Forest remains the warm default.
Do use sunshine (#f7d76e) only for what is live, pressed or just happened, and peach (#f9ceb0) for warmth and the softer option.
Do use Baloo 800 for anything named or chosen and Nunito for anything explained; keep everything sentence case.
Do make stage controls full pills with floor shadows (negative spread, black at low alpha) and no borders; keep parent controls at 10 to 16 px corners with 1 px lines.

Do keep targets at 44 px in the parent room, 52 px for stage pills and 64 px for the child's answers and keypad keys; every actionable control keeps a visible focus ring (ochre on cream, sunshine on forest).
Do let the world fill the viewport in the Studio with chrome floating at a 16 px edge and the lab beside the world, never over it.
Do ease Studio entrances with `cubic-bezier(0.22, 1, 0.36, 1)`; keep acting discrete and requested gestures bounded, with semantic poses and feedback retained under `prefers-reduced-motion`.
Do mount registered preset actor art in the existing fixed square SVG slot so optional Rive assets swap without layout change.
Do use shared registered raster poses for predefined actors, preserve Tooth Town and coach matching poses, tie travel locomotion to actual distance, and keep Pip in its reserved dock tile.
Do retain the cream-and-forest Learn shell while generated art supplies tactile material and light.
donts: Don't put a heading, a card frame or a scrolling column over or around the world in the Studio.

Don't use yellow on a resting interface surface. Learn paintings may contain their subjects’ natural colors; its scene washes are the documented readability exception to the Studio’s spotlight-and-spell gradient guidance.
Don't add uppercase labels, letter-spaced eyebrows or kicker lines; small labels get Baloo weight and a darker colour instead.
Don't use hard offset shadows, even glows or coloured halos on resting elements.
Don’t add page-specific palettes or freeform CSS themes; the authorized Forest, Ocean and Terracotta presets change existing roles together.
Don't present the geometric landing window or local registered raster cast as final external Rive assets. Delivered local artwork has its own documented limits.
Don't describe sprite acting as finished film, a continuous skeletal rig or phoneme lip-sync, or claim pose coverage for single-image photos/outfits or old generated worlds.
Don't replace inline SVG icons with glyph fonts or emoji in chrome.
Do not reintroduce decorative sparkle control symbols, summon particles, guide-name sparks or a voice-off particle halo; retain semantic stars and purposeful contained voice feedback.
